lesson.intro: A sentence is a group of words that makes complete sense. Words must be in the [[right order]].
points: A sentence begins with a [[capital letter]].
It ends with a full stop ( . ), a question mark ( ? ) or an exclamation mark ( ! ).
Most sentences follow this order: [[Who / What]] + [[doing word]] + the rest. Example: The cat + drinks + milk.
Questions often start with a question word or a helping verb: Where is…? Can you…? Do you…?
Describing words come before the noun: a [[red]] ball, the [[tall]] boy.

examples.note: time words often go at the end

lesson.tip: Find the word with the capital letter – it usually starts the sentence. Find the word with the full stop – it usually ends it.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is in the correct order?
options: We are going to Penang tomorrow.
We going are to Penang tomorrow.
Tomorrow going we are to Penang.
We are to going Penang tomorrow.
questions.answer: We are going to Penang tomorrow.
questions.explanation: "are going" stays together.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is in the correct order?
options: The old man walked slowly to the mosque.
The old man slowly walked the mosque to.
Walked the old man slowly to the mosque.
The man old walked slowly to the mosque.
questions.answer: The old man walked slowly to the mosque.
questions.explanation: The describing word "old" comes before "man".

questions.prompt: Which sentence has the correct punctuation?
questions.answer: Where are you going, Amin?
questions.explanation: Capital letter at the start, capital for the name, and a question mark at the end.
